headline_hint: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announces closure amid state pressure

raw_model_output.headline: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta closes after state pressure
raw_model_output.body:
Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced its closure after being evicted from its central Moscow office [c51][c60]. Landlords told staff they must vacate the newsroom of 30 years by November 9 [c51][c60]. Authorities also blocked the newspaper from receiving reader donations [c51].

Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov wrote on the website that the newspaper was in a kill zone after nearly five years of working while surrounded by security services [c56]. Police questioned Sokolov and searched his home earlier in 2026 [c55]. That search was connected to investigative journalist Oleg Roldugin, who was arrested and charged with unlawful access to computerized information [c54].

Six Novaya Gazeta journalists have been killed over the years, including Anna Politkovskaya, who was shot dead in October 2006 [c53]. Co-founder Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021 [c52]. Russian authorities labeled him a foreign agent in 2023 [c52]. Someone doused Muratov with red paint on a train in April 2022, which damaged his eyesight [c58]. After Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, the newspaper printed blank white spaces to show censored text [c57]. Exiled journalists set up Novaya Gazeta Europe [c59].

claims_available.text: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced its closure after being evicted from its office of 30 years and blocked from receiving reader donations.
Novaya Gazeta co-founder Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021 and was designated a foreign agent by Russian authorities in 2023.
Six Novaya Gazeta journalists have been killed over the years, including Anna Politkovskaya who was shot dead in October 2006.
Novaya Gazeta investigative journalist Oleg Roldugin was arrested earlier in 2026 and charged with unlawful access to computerized information.
Novaya Gazeta editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov was questioned by police and had his home searched in connection with Roldugin's case.
Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov wrote on Novaya Gazeta's website that the newspaper found itself in a kill zone after nearly five years of working while encircled by security services.
Following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Novaya Gazeta published blank white spaces in print to indicate censored text.
Dmitry Muratov was doused with red paint while on a train in April 2022, causing damage to his eyesight.
Exiled Novaya Gazeta journalists set up Novaya Gazeta Europe, while Muratov's team in Russia printed magazines with runs of 999 copies to bypass official licensing requirements.
Landlords informed Novaya Gazeta staff that they must vacate their central Moscow office newsroom by November 9.
